function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** you can follow to get everything set up.  
I’ll include the exact files you’ll need to create (Dockerfile, Kubernetes YAML, GitHub Actions workflow) and the Git commands to commit & push them.

> **NOTE** – I don’t have direct access to your machine or the internet, so you’ll need to run the commands yourself.  
> If you run into any errors, feel free to ask for clarification.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> *If you’re using HTTPS instead of SSH, replace the URL accordingly.*

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the Repo & Create/Update Files

### 2.1 Inspect the Project

Run `ls -R` or open the folder in your editor.  
Typical Node.js projects contain:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `package.json` | Dependencies & scripts |
| `app.js` or `index.js` | Entry point |
| `.env` | Environment variables (optional) |

> **Tip:** Look at the `scripts.start` entry in `package.json`. That tells us what command starts the server.

### 2.2 Create/Update the Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` in the repo root with the following content:

```dockerfile
# Use official Node runtime as a parent image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Set working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package.json and package-lock.json first
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the application code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * `node:18-alpine` is lightweight and stable.  
> * `npm ci` ensures reproducible installs.  
> * `EXPOSE 3000` matches the typical port for Node apps; adjust if your app uses a different one.

### 2.3 Create Kubernetes YAML

Create a file named `k8s-deployment.yaml` in the repo root:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # Update if you use another registry
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **What this does**  
> * Deploys two replicas of the container.  
> * Exposes the app via a LoadBalancer (adjust `type` if you’re on a cluster without LB support).  
> * Maps external port 80 to internal port 3000.

### 2.4 Create GitHub Actions Workflow

Create a file at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout source
      uses: actions/checkout@v3

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v2

    - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
      uses: docker/login-action@v2
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build and push Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        push: true
        tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest
```

> **How it works**  
> * Triggers on pushes to `main`.  
> * Builds the Docker image from the repo root.  
> * Pushes the image to GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io`).  
> * Uses the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN` for authentication (no extra secrets needed).

---

## 3️⃣ Add All Changed Files to Git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s-deployment.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & Push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run and build/push the Docker image.

---

## 🎉 What’s Next?

* **Deploy to Kubernetes** – Once the image is available in GHCR, you can apply the manifest:

  ```bash
  kubectl apply -f k8s-deployment.yaml
  ```

* **Expose the Service** – If you’re on a cloud provider, the LoadBalancer will provision an external IP.  
  Check status with:

  ```bash
  kubectl get svc nodejs-welcome
  ```

* **Monitor Logs** – View pod logs:

  ```bash
  kubectl logs -f deployment/nodejs-welcome
  ```

---

### Troubleshooting Tips

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| Docker build fails due to missing `app.js` | Verify the entry point file exists and matches the CMD in Dockerfile. |
| Kubernetes deployment stuck in `ContainerCreating` | Check image pull errors: `kubectl describe pod <pod-name>` |
| GitHub Actions fails to log in to GHCR | Ensure the repo has the `GITHUB_TOKEN` secret (it’s built‑in). |
| Port mismatch | Adjust `EXPOSE` in Dockerfile and `containerPort` in Kubernetes YAML to match your app’s listening port. |

Feel free to reach out if you hit any snags!
